summary: Defines three new DHCP options that deliver configuration information to clients of Novell Directory Services, such as which servers and directory tree to use. This lets such clients configure themselves automatically when joining a network.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2241 defines DHCP options for telling a Novell Directory Services client which servers and directory tree to use. The options can also provide an initial context within that tree.

subtitle: Three DHCP options that configure a Novell Directory Services client.

tldr.problem: An NDS client needs to locate a directory server and choose a useful starting point in its directory tree.
tldr.mechanism: DHCP options provide a list of NDS servers, the NDS tree name, and an initial directory context, with the text encoded as UTF-8.
tldr.outcome: The options give an NDS client enough information to connect to a tree without manual configuration.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 2241's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines DHCP options for configuring clients of Novell Directory Services.

sections.title: Information an NDS Client Needs
sections.content:
Novell Directory Services is a distributed, replicated directory of network objects. An NDS client needs to locate a server to authenticate and access the directory, and it benefits from starting near the part of the directory likely to matter to its user.

This RFC defines three DHCP options to carry that setup information: a list of NDS servers, an NDS tree name, and an initial NDS context.
sections.plainLanguage: A client needs a directory server and a place to start looking in the directory. DHCP can provide both during network configuration.

sections.title: The NDS Servers Option
sections.content:
The NDS Servers option carries one or more server addresses for the client to contact. Servers should be listed in preference order.

The option code is 85. Its minimum length is 4 octets, and its length must be a multiple of 4 because the data contains server addresses.
sections.plainLanguage: This option gives the client a list of directory servers to try. The order can show which server is preferred.

sections.title: Tree Name and Initial Context
sections.content:
The NDS Tree Name option uses code 86 and carries the tree name as UTF-8-encoded octets. The NDS Context option uses code 87 and carries the initial context in the same encoding; neither string should end with a zero byte.

Each context option can hold at most 255 octets. A longer context can be split across multiple instances, whose contents are concatenated; even one encoded character may be split between instances.
sections.plainLanguage: The tree name and starting context are sent as UTF-8 text. A long context can span several DHCP options that the client joins together.
